resources.string:
1. Apply the sensor.
2. Type the 4-digit code or scan the code on the applicator. Do this now, do not wait for the warm-up.
3. Press Scan, select your sensor, then press Connect.
4. Accept the Android pairing request if it shows.

Warm-up takes about 30 minutes for a new sensor.
After Connect the warm-up screen opens. The countdown also shows on the overview and in the notification, so you do not have to stay on that screen.
Type the 4-digit code, or scan the code on the applicator.

string.name: dexcom_oneplus_applicator_parsed
string.comment: %1$s=4-digit pairing code, %2$s=serial or dash. Example: Code 1234 · serial ABCD

resources.string: Before pairing: allow nearby Bluetooth devices (and notifications if asked). Keep the phone near the sensor during start and warm-up.

Every G7 / ONE+ sensor in range is listed. The 4-digit code is not sent in the Bluetooth signal, so the app cannot use it to find your sensor. Pick the one you have just applied. The code is checked when you press Connect.

string.name: dexcom_oneplus_scan_idle
string.comment: %1$d=number of devices found. Example: 2

resources.string: Select a sensor from the scan list
This is a different sensor from the paired one, but the pairing code has not changed. Type or scan the new code, or press Connect again to keep the current one.

Only one app can use the sensor over Bluetooth. Stop the Dexcom app, xDrip+ and Juggluco first, or turn off their sensor connection. AAPS joins a running sensor and does not end it. It is not certain that the Dexcom app can use the sensor again afterwards.
Enter a valid 4-digit sensor pairing code
Bluetooth permission is required before starting the sensor

On: a finger prick value is sent to the sensor itself, as the Dexcom app does. The sensor keeps it, and it cannot be edited or deleted. Off: the value is used to correct readings inside the app, and can be removed later.
The sensor accepts a finger prick value from 40 to 400 mg/dL (2.2 to 22.2 mmol/L) only.
This finger prick value is more than one hour old. Measure again.
The sensor is still warming up, or has stopped. Calibrate when it shows readings again.
No sensor reading in the last 10 minutes. Wait for the next reading, then try again.
The sensor did not give a trend with its last reading. Wait for the next reading, then try again.
Glucose is changing too fast. Calibrate when it is stable.
The value could not be sent to the sensor. The sensor may be out of range, still warming up, or another value may still be on its way.
No finger prick value has been sent to this sensor yet.
Your value is waiting to be sent to the sensor. It goes out the next time the app and the sensor talk, which is usually within a few minutes.
The sensor says it took your value.
The sensor says it did not take your value. Your reading was not changed.

The sensor did not give a clear answer, so it is not possible to say whether your value was used. It is not an app error and it is not a success. Do not send the value again. Compare the sensor with a finger prick within the next hour before you rely on its readings, and ask your care team if you are unsure.
Your value was not sent to the sensor. Nothing reached the sensor, so you can enter the value again.
The sensor or its connection changed before the value went out.

resources.string: This is the app\'s own timer of about 30 minutes, because the sensor has not sent the time left yet.
Connecting over Bluetooth. Keep the app open and stay close to the sensor. This can take up to a minute.
No loop glucose yet — wait until warm-up finishes.
The sensor accepted the code. Starting readings…
The connection to the sensor ended.
The sensor did not accept the code, or Bluetooth pairing failed. Accept the Android pairing request and try again.

string.name: dexcom_oneplus_error_refused_stopped
string.comment: %1$d=how many refusals in a row, for example 3

resources.string: The sensor refused this phone %1$d times in a row. AAPS stopped trying, because one more refusal locks the sensor for a while. Check the pairing code, close the Dexcom app, xDrip+ or Juggluco if one of them uses the sensor, then start the sensor again.
The sensor refused this phone. AAPS waits 15 minutes before it asks again, because refusals in a row lock the sensor. Check the pairing code and close other apps that use the sensor.
Connection or sensor session error. Check the Bluetooth connection and try again.
If the problem continues, open the driver log on this screen.
Ongoing sensor connection and warm-up status.
This sensor is already your pre-soak sensor

It is running as your pre-soak sensor. One sensor cannot be paired twice at the same time: the two connections would disturb each other and the pairing fails for both.\n\nIf it is ready, switch to it. That keeps everything it has collected. Otherwise cancel the pre-soak, which deletes what it has collected, and start it here instead.
Dexcom G7 / ONE+ is switched off. Select it as BG source in Configuration first, then try again.
This sensor already feeds the loop. Start it as the main sensor, not as a pre-soak.

string.name: dexcom_oneplus_notif_waiting_adv
string.comment: %1$d = whole minutes the sensor has been silent. Example: No signal from the sensor for 7 min

resources.string: No signal from the sensor for %1$d min — keep the phone close
Another Dexcom G7 / ONE+ sensor is nearby but the paired one stays silent. Start the sensor again to pair the new one.
Keep the phone near the sensor

The main sensor feeds the loop after warm-up. A pre-soak sensor is a second sensor that warms up next to the sensor in use. It only collects readings, and never feeds the loop until you switch to it from the status screen.

The pre-soak sensor collects readings in the background and does not feed the loop. Go back to the overview, and switch to it later, from the overview or the G7 / ONE+ status screen, when it is ready.
No reading yet. The pre-soak sensor is still warming up or out of range.
The loop will use the pre-soak sensor from now on, and the sensor in use is stopped. This cannot be undone.
Use this only if the sensor in use has stopped or has to be replaced now. The pre-soak sensor is reading, but it has not finished its 12 hour settling time.
Switch to a sensor that is not settled?

The pre-soak sensor is sending readings, but it has not finished its 12 hour settling time. Its readings can be less accurate for the first hours, so the loop may dose on values that are too high or too low. Only do this if the sensor in use has stopped or must be replaced now. This switches the loop\'s glucose source and cannot be undone.
The pre-soak sensor now feeds the loop.
The switch was made, but older calibration entries could not be ignored. Remove finger prick calibrations taken before this switch, then calibrate again if needed.

The switch was made, but reconnecting the sensor failed. The sensor in use is now the one that was the pre-soak sensor. Open the G7 / ONE+ status screen and bring the sensor back in range. This is not a complete success.
A step after the switch failed, and the app does not know which sensor is in use. This is not a complete success. Open the G7 / ONE+ status screen and check which sensor is in use.
There is no pre-soak sensor to switch to.
The pre-soak sensor has not settled long enough yet.
The pre-soak sensor has not sent enough valid readings yet.
The pre-soak sensor has not sent a reading in the last minutes. Wait until it reads again before switching to it.
Before you pair: other sensor apps

string.name: dexcom_oneplus_scan_slot_held
string.comment: Short label under a sensor in the scan list. Another phone or app is connected to this sensor now.

resources.string: Other sensor apps on this phone

These apps are installed and can connect to the sensor themselves. A sensor talks to one app at a time, so the sensor may refuse AAPS while one of them uses it. Close it or turn off its sensor connection before you start. AAPS joins a running sensor and does not end it. It is not certain that the Dexcom app can use the sensor again afterwards.
